attempts.summary: Configured tc/HTB traffic shaping on node1 (OpenWrt router) to cap throughput to/from node2 (10.100.237.11) at ~1Mbit/s in each direction, while leaving node1's other traffic (e.g. to node3) unshaped. Egress shaping uses an HTB class filtered on dst=node2's IP on br-lan; ingress shaping redirects src=node2 traffic to an IFB device with a matching 1mbit HTB class. Config persisted via a new /etc/init.d/tc-node2-shape boot script (S99/K10). Demonstrated the limit with real 8MB SCP transfers between node2 and node1 in both directions (~70.4s each ≈ 0.95Mbit/s), and proved node1's traffic to node3 is unaffected (a 300-packet/1400B ping burst to node3 completed in ~10ms, routed through the unshaped default HTB class with zero overlimits, vs. class 1:10 for node2 which showed overlimit throttling). Completed the mandatory restart-evidence protocol: captured boot_id baselines on all three nodes, restarted each one at a time (node1 then node2 then node3) via native reboot, confirmed boot_id changed after each restart, and verified recovery (tc shaping/ifb/dropbear alive on node1; network/services active and repeat SCP test still shaped correctly on node2; sshd active on node3). All temporary test files and injected SSH keys were cleaned up afterward.
